findings.pdf_says: (page 20, folio xii, ends after the table of contents line "INDEX ... XVIII-1" and the folio "xii"; the heading "SECTION I:  INTRODUCTORY INFORMATION" is printed only on page 21, folio I-1)
findings.why_it_matters: A stray level-1 heading follows the folio of page 20, duplicating the section heading that page 21 carries (as "## <u>SECTION I: INTRODUCTORY INFORMATION</u>"). Page 20 prints no such heading; the document now has two SECTION I headings at different levels, one under the wrong page.

findings.pdf_says: 1.3  ORGANIZATION OF DOCUMENT ... 1.4  HOW TO USE THE STANDARD
findings.markdown_says: ## 1.3 ORGANIZATION OF DOCUMENT ... ## 1.4 HOW TO USE THE STANDARD
findings.why_it_matters: Wrong heading level: 1.3 and 1.4 are subclauses of clause 1 (INTRODUCTION TO THE STANDARD), printed in the same style as 1.1 and 1.2, which page 21 transcribes as "### 1.1 SCOPE AND PURPOSE" and "### 1.2 STRUCTURE OF LANGUAGE SPECIFICATIONS". At "##" they sit at the same level as "## 1. INTRODUCTION TO THE STANDARD" and the section heading, so the outline detaches them from clause 1.

findings.pdf_says: The elements of the Debug module are divided into two levels.
findings.markdown_says: The elements or the Debug module are divided into two levels.
findings.why_it_matters: The printed word is "of" (its f faintly struck, so it looks like "ot"), parallel to every sibling paragraph ("The elements of the Segmentation module are divided into two levels."). The transcription reads it as "or", which makes the sentence ungrammatical.
